sources: JMA bosai typhoon feed (targetTc.json + specifications.json), read 6 Sep 2026 22:12 UTC (7 Sep JST, issue 06:45). One active system worldwide: TC2628 Krovanh, storm No. 2624, category TS. Analysis position 26.2N 131.5E, about 50 km north-northeast of Minamidaito, moving north-northeast at 10 km/h, central pressure 990 hPa, sustained winds 18 m/s gusting 25 m/s, gale radius 330 km. JMA forecasts it to weaken to a tropical depression by +12h (27.6N 133.0E) and to reach 29.3N 132.8E by +24h, tracking away from the China coast toward the open Pacific east of Kyushu. Closest approach to any tracked port across all analysis and forecast points is Busan at 735 km on the +24h point; Shanghai/Ningbo is 1,062 km, Xiamen 1,362 km, Qingdao 1,393 km. All outside the 600 km threshold, so no threats are scored this run. TC2621 Saudel is no longer in the JMA active feed.

SEKO Asia-Pacific Logistics Monitoring Center, Week 36 update, last updated Friday 4 September 2026 10:00 HKT. Shanghai (CNSHA): open, severe backlog; Waigaoqiao WGQ2 and WGQ5 waiting 9+ days, Yangshan YS12 7+ days, after 54-hour (Yangshan) and 48-hour (Waigaoqiao) closures earlier in the week; barge resources critically tight into the Yangtze corridor. Ningbo-Zhoushan (CNNGB): reopened after a cumulative 78 hours of closure over the past week; Meishan MSICT yard density above 90%, MSICT average waiting 5-6 days (3-4 days for mega-vessels over 366m LOA); terminals have asked lines to hold local export rolling ratios below 10%. Xiamen (CMXMN): fully open after a brief 6.6-hour closure on 3 September. Yantian (CNYTN): 3-4 days for smaller vessels, 4-5 days for vessels over 330m LOA, expected to ease only after Golden Week. Qingdao (CNTAO): operating smoothly with a 0.5-day wait; QQCTU berth dredging until 10 September, QQCTN thereafter through year-end. Hong Kong: HIT average wait 1.5-2 days, yard utilisation above 85%.

MSC customer advisories (msc.com/en/newsroom/customer-advisories) checked 6 Sep 2026 via Chrome. No port-closure or weather-suspension notice for any tracked Asian port; most recent entries are Golden Week sailing programmes (24 and 26 Aug), a Red Sea service resumption (24 Aug) and price announcements. Nothing contradicts the SEKO picture.

Shanghai/Ningbo.note: Terminals at both ports are open and have been since 28 August. What is left is queue, not closure, and the queue is still getting worse: Linerlytica's 4 September snapshot puts 1.58M TEU on 264 ships at anchorage off Shanghai/Ningbo with a queue-to-berth ratio of 3.02, up from 2.95 the day before and the highest of any tracked port by a factor of six. The headline range has narrowed from 6-10 days last run to 5-9, but that improvement is at Ningbo (MSICT 5-6 days) rather than Shanghai, where Waigaoqiao is still quoting 9+ days. The two ports each lost 48-78 hours of working time in the week to 4 September, and barge capacity into the Yangtze corridor is the binding constraint on clearing it. Krovanh is the named active system but has turned north-northeast, is 1,062 km away and is weakening to a depression, so it is no longer adding closures here; it is carried as the primary event only because it is the system still on the board while the backlog it and Saudel created remains unresolved. Golden Week loading is the next pressure point.

remarks: One active tropical cyclone in the JMA feed: TS Krovanh, weakening to a depression within 12 hours and tracking north-northeast away from China. Closest approach to any tracked port is Busan at 735 km, outside the 600 km threshold, so no threat rows are scored and the incoming-systems table is empty this run.

Xiamen and Shenzhen (Yantian) have been dropped. Both were carried as 'watch' on Typhoon Saudel with eventEnded 2026-09-03, so their two-day grace window closed on 5 September. Saudel is gone from the JMA feed, Xiamen reopened after a 6.6-hour closure on 3 September, and Yantian's remaining 3-5 day wait is Golden Week peak-season bunching rather than weather. Dropping Yantian also restores the site's own berths-idle flag for that port, which is now the right signal.
Shanghai/Ningbo is the only live entry and it is the one that matters: 1.58M TEU at anchorage against 241K at Singapore, the next largest. Its queue-to-berth ratio rose again on 4 September to 3.02.

Expiry warning for the next run: this entry survives on its primary event name matching an active system, and Krovanh is forecast to drop to a tropical depression within 12 hours and will likely leave the JMA active feed. When it does the entry falls back to the age of 'since' (26 Aug) and expires immediately, taking the largest congestion story on the board off the page. If the backlog is still unresolved next run, re-anchor the event to whatever system is then current, or accept the expiry deliberately — do not let it lapse by accident.
Linerlytica's public window now runs 21 August to 4 September and has caught up after the gap that stalled it at 30 August last week; five new dates were merged.

No source states a berth waiting time for Busan, Qingdao, Haiphong, Ho Chi Minh City, Laem Chabang or Singapore this run, so none is recorded. Qingdao is explicitly reported as normal at a 0.5-day wait and is therefore omitted rather than listed as open.
